description: The module's public face: the domain Caddy serves it on, how it is reached upstream, and who is allowed to reach it.
_note: update-service.sh already reconciles this properly against Caddy's own model: it creates a missing domain/handler and, when the handler configuration has changed, DELETES AND RECREATES it. That compare-and-recreate is one atomic decision across several fields — a generic per-field differ would have to re-derive it and could not express 'the handler as a whole is different'. So every field is apply:'reconcile' and the existing logic stays. What the manifest adds is the change CLASS, which is what makes 'modify --set proxyPort=8443' a sanctioned operation instead of a hand-edit (#557).

proxyDomain.note: The public hostname. Changing it re-issues the ACME certificate and moves the handler; the module itself is untouched, so no guest downtime — though clients on the old name stop resolving as soon as DNS follows.

proxyPort.note: The upstream port Caddy forwards to. A handler rewrite, applied live.

proxyUpstreamTls.note: Whether the hop from Caddy to the module is itself TLS. Declared as a string in module-fields.json, so the boolean normalizer is what makes 'true' and true one value.

proxyUpstreamHttp1.note: Force HTTP/1.1 upstream, for a backend that cannot speak h2c.

proxyPreserveHost.note: Pass the original Host header through, for a backend that generates absolute URLs from it.

proxyTls.note: Which certificate strategy serves the domain (per-service or the environment wildcard).

proxyAllowedZones.note: Which zones may reach the published name — the difference between an internal service and one exposed to the internet. A live firewall/Caddy change, and the field most worth being able to set through a verb rather than by hand.

firewallType.note: Which firewall implementation serves this estate. 'NONE' makes the service print manual instructions instead of calling a controller; that branch is the non-field logic update-service.sh keeps.

aliasType.note: How the module is addressed in the generated firewall alias (host vs network).
